findings.paper_title: Item 9. Appendix 1 Internal Audit Progress report August 2026
findings.headline: Accounts payable function has 162 unreconciled transactions worth approximately £55,000 from activity over a year old.
findings.detail: The audit of accounts payable (delivered by Cambridgeshire County Council under a lead authority model) found that 162 transactions totalling around £55,000 remained unreconciled across four councils, with the activity dating back over a year. Additionally, three reconciliations lacked required compliance review completion, and gaps were found in independent checks for two bank account detail changes.
findings.matters: Unreconciled transactions of this age represent a potential control weakness and create risk of misstatement in the accounts or undetected fraud. The fact they remain unreconciled after a year suggests either control breakdowns or inadequate monitoring.
findings.figures: 162 unreconciled transactions; approximately £55,000; activity dating over a year ago; 3 missing compliance reviews
findings.quote: The review of ZAP15 (returned or refunded payments) control account reconciliations found that whilst the level of unreconciled items was judged as low both given the overall level / value of transactions processed for each Council, 162 transactions were found across the four councils, equating to around £55,000 that were unreconciled and related to activity generated over a year ago.

findings.paper_title: Item 9. Appendix 1 Internal Audit Progress report August 2026
findings.headline: Member development control environment rated Moderate (Amber), indicating gaps in internal control framework.
findings.detail: The audit of member development gave a Moderate (Amber) assurance rating for both control environment and compliance, meaning there are gaps in the internal control framework posing medium risk. Specific issues include: the Member Development Plan is at draft stage with unclear contribution to expected outcomes; progress assessment expectations are not defined; a 50% attendance target for non-mandatory training lacks clear justification and has not been reviewed recently; and reporting of mandatory training attendance has been underreported.
findings.matters: A council's governance framework depends on elected members being properly trained and developed. Control gaps here mean the council may lack assurance that decision-makers have the knowledge to properly discharge their responsibilities, which weakens corporate governance and poses risk to financial stewardship.
findings.figures: Moderate (Amber) rating for control environment and compliance; two-thirds of members elected in 2025 were new to role
findings.quote: Based upon the fieldwork completed, the following assurance opinions have been given: Internal Audit Assurance Opinion Control Environment Moderate (Amber) Satisfactory Compliance Moderate (Amber)

findings.paper_title: Item 9. Appendix 1 Internal Audit Progress report August 2026
findings.headline: Two high-priority audit recommendations remain overdue for implementation, with 38 total recommendations still outstanding.
findings.detail: As of 29 July 2026, 38 audit recommendations across all priority levels are overdue for implementation, down from 63 in June. Of these, two are rated high priority and are less than three months overdue. This indicates the council is not promptly addressing findings from internal audits and previously identified control weaknesses.
findings.matters: A lender needs to know that identified control gaps are being closed. A growing backlog of overdue audit recommendations signals that the council's governance response to identified risks is sluggish, which is a red flag for financial management.
findings.figures: 38 recommendations overdue; 2 high-priority actions overdue; down from 63 overdue in June 2026
findings.quote: There are 38 recommendations overdue for implementation as at 29th July 2026, this is a reduction from 63 overdue actions as reported in the progress report in June 2026. There are two high priority actions overdue for implementation. Of these, all are less than three months overdue.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A (REVISED) Annual Governance Statement 25-26 - Pre Approval
findings.headline: Mandatory training compliance remains incomplete and inconsistent across the workforce, identified as a recurring audit theme
findings.detail: Internal Audit flagged gaps in workforce mandatory training completion as a continuing issue across service areas. The council acknowledges this requires improvement and is rolling out bespoke leadership training on governance basics.
findings.matters: Gaps in mandatory training (likely including fraud awareness, safeguarding, financial controls) suggest staff may not be aware of compliance obligations, amplifying control risk.
findings.figures: Identified as a recurring audit theme; completion rates not stated
findings.quote: Internal Audit identified mandatory training compliance as a recurring theme, with inconsistent completion across some service areas.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A (REVISED) Annual Governance Statement 25-26 - Pre Approval
findings.headline: Only 71% of audit recommendations due in 2025-26 were completed; some actions remain overdue by more than three months
findings.detail: Internal Audit reports that implementation of agreed remedial actions lags behind schedule, with a portion outstanding beyond agreed timescales. This is a governance execution gap rather than a policy gap.
findings.matters: If the council struggles to implement its own identified improvements, identified risks persist longer and governance maturity is lower. This extends the tail risk from control weaknesses.
findings.figures: 71% implementation rate; some actions overdue by more than three months
findings.quote: A proportion of agreed internal audit actions remain outstanding, including some overdue by more than three months, indicating that further focus is required to ensure timely implementation.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A (REVISED) Annual Governance Statement 25-26 - Pre Approval
findings.headline: Internal Audit identified two areas of Limited Assurance relating to safeguarding and licensing compliance, with gaps in DBS checks and safeguarding record-keeping
findings.detail: Audit found inconsistencies in 'fit and proper person' checks in taxi licensing (including DBS check gaps) and gaps in safeguarding checks for home-to-school transport providers. These are operational control failures in compliance-critical areas.
findings.matters: Control failures in safeguarding suggest broader control execution maturity issues; they carry legal and reputational risk beyond the immediate scope.
findings.figures: 2 Limited Assurance opinions out of 76 audit opinions issued; 97% of audits achieved Moderate Assurance or above
findings.quote: Weaknesses in the application and evidencing of 'fit and proper person' checks in taxi licensing, including inconsistencies in Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) checks and right-to-work verification.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A (REVISED) Annual Governance Statement 25-26 - Pre Approval
findings.headline: Dedicated Schools Grant deficit and special educational needs costs are identified as ongoing key financial risks requiring continued focus
findings.detail: The AGS explicitly names DSG deficit as a material risk to financial resilience and long-term sustainability, appearing across multiple governance sections. This suggests it is structural rather than transient.
findings.matters: DSG deficits accumulate and reduce future spending flexibility; repeated identification as a key risk indicates lack of viable solution to date.
findings.figures: DSG deficit (specific figures not provided in this excerpt)
findings.quote: In particular, the Dedicated Schools Grant (DSG) deficit and costs associated with special educational needs and children's services remain key financial risks, requiring continued focus and robust management arrangements.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A (REVISED) Annual Governance Statement 25-26 - Pre Approval
findings.headline: The Council faced an overall revenue overspend in 2025-26, covered through in-year management action and use of earmarked reserves
findings.detail: Demand-led services, particularly adults and children's social care, created budget pressures that resulted in total overspend. The council partially mitigated this through management action and drawing on earmarked reserves. This indicates the budget was insufficient for actual demand.
findings.matters: Lenders assess whether a council is running on underlying balance or reserves; repeated reserve usage signals unsustainable budget positions. This suggests structural mismatch between budget and demand.
findings.figures: Overall overspend (specific amount not stated in this excerpt)
findings.quote: These pressures resulted in an overall overspend against the approved budget, which was partially mitigated through in-year management action and the use of earmarked reserves.

findings.paper_title: Capital Programme Update 2026/27
findings.headline: Two-thirds of capital programme depends on grant funding with timing and eligibility risks
findings.detail: £208.6m of the £308.6m programme (67.6%) is grant-funded. The council explicitly acknowledges risks from third-party funding, particularly around meeting funder criteria and meeting payment deadlines.
findings.matters: Lenders need to understand funding security. If grant conditions are not met or deadlines missed, the council may need alternative funding quickly or descope projects, affecting service delivery and financial stability.
findings.figures: Grant funding £208.6m; S106 contributions £5.8m; other contributions £0.6m; total £308.6m
findings.quote: There is a risk in relation to funding, particularly where it is from third parties including grants. Appropriate agreements must be entered into to ensure that the funding is secured and spend is in accordance with any criteria stipulated by the funder, this includes both the nature of the spend and the timing (where a deadline applies).

findings.paper_title: Capital Programme Update 2026/27
findings.headline: Rising interest rates may reduce future capital programme affordability
findings.detail: The council identifies that current economic conditions are increasing borrowing costs. This treasury risk affects overall programme affordability and may necessitate a reduced capital programme in future years.
findings.matters: A lender assessing the council's capital investment capacity and medium-term financial stability needs to know that rising rates directly reduce what the council can afford to borrow for future capital schemes.
findings.figures: Current programme includes no new borrowing; funded from grants (£208.6m), capital receipts (£15.6m), discretionary sources (£77.9m)
findings.quote: The current uncertain economic context is also increasing interest rates associated with borrowing that is used to fund elements of the capital programme. This treasury risk impacts the overall affordability of the programme, which will be closely monitored and managed, but may lead to a reduced capital programme in the future.

findings.paper_title: Capital Programme Update 2026/27
findings.headline: Inflation above original bid levels risks forcing project scope reductions
findings.detail: The council explicitly acknowledges that cost-of-living inflation has driven price rises significantly higher than in previous periods and above the original funding bid levels. This poses a risk to project deliverability, potentially requiring descoping of projects rather than allowing overspends.
findings.matters: A lender needs confidence the council can deliver its planned capital investment. If inflation forces scope cuts, the council delivers less infrastructure than planned and may face unmet service delivery expectations.
findings.figures: £308.6m total programme (up £30.6m from £278m); Place £224.0m, Children's Services £68.8m
findings.quote: This therefore poses a risk to the deliverability of the projects as originally envisaged, where reductions to the scope of projects may be required to ensure budgets are not overspent.

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item No 5 Appendix A - Annual Internal Audit Report and Opinion 2025
findings.headline: Limited Assurance given for taxi licensing fit-and-proper person checks; compliance gaps in Disclosure and Barring Service checks for home-to-school transport
findings.detail: Internal audit gave Limited Assurance (indicating high risk) for taxi licensing compliance, citing gaps in evidencing right-to-work checks and inconsistent application of six-monthly DBS re-check policy. Home-to-school transport providers similarly received Limited Assurance for control design due to record-keeping errors and failure to conduct DBS checks in line with update service requirements. Both areas represent failures to apply safeguarding controls consistently.
findings.matters: Failures in DBS and right-to-work compliance create regulatory and legal liability risk for the Council, including potential fines, enforcement action, and claims arising from inadequate safeguarding—matters that affect both reputation and financial exposure.
findings.figures: Taxi licensing: Limited Assurance for compliance; Home-to-school transport: Limited Assurance for control design
findings.quote: Limited Assurance was given by Internal Audit in relation to compliance with controls for 'fit and proper person' checks on taxi licence holders, primarily in relation to evidencing compliant right to work checks and applying the Council's policy on six monthly Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) re-checks

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item No 5 Appendix A - Annual Internal Audit Report and Opinion 2025
findings.headline: Year-end financial assurance not yet finalised for shared service systems covering accounts receivable and debt recovery
findings.detail: The Council operates accounts receivable and debt recovery through shared service arrangements under a lead authority model with other councils. At the time of reporting, internal audit could not provide assurance over these systems because year-end assessments had not yet been completed by the partner authorities. This creates a material gap in the financial systems assurance coverage.
findings.matters: Accounts receivable and debt recovery are core income-generating systems that affect cash flow and bad debt provisions; lack of assurance over these systems leaves material uncertainty about the effectiveness of income collection controls.
findings.figures: Accounts receivable and debt recovery systems: assurance not yet finalised at time of reporting
findings.quote: This must be caveated in that year end assurances have not yet been finalised in relation to the shared service financial systems for accounts receivable and debt recovery, which operate under the shared service, lead authority model. As such, assurance cannot be given over those systems at the time of reporting

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item No 5 Appendix A - Annual Internal Audit Report and Opinion 2025
findings.headline: 21% of agreed management actions are overdue by more than 3 months, with only 71% of due actions completed in 2025/26
findings.detail: Of 211 agreed management actions from audits, 150 (71%) were implemented during the year. However, 45 actions (21%) remain overdue—agreed and due over 3 months ago but still not completed—alongside a further 16 actions (8%) that are within the last 3 months of their deadline and also unimplemented. This indicates material implementation risk in addressing identified control weaknesses.
findings.matters: Slow implementation of corrective actions demonstrates execution risk; identified control weaknesses persist longer, multiplying exposure and suggesting management capacity or priority issues in addressing audit findings.
findings.figures: 150 of 211 actions implemented (71%); 45 actions (21%) overdue 3+ months; 16 actions (8%) due within last 3 months but not implemented
findings.quote: Of the recommended actions agreed during 2025/26, and due for implementation, 71% had been completed during the year.

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item No 5 Appendix A - Annual Internal Audit Report and Opinion 2025
findings.headline: External auditors identified two significant weaknesses in the Council's ability to develop sufficient savings plans and manage the Dedicated Schools Grant deficit
findings.detail: Grant Thornton highlighted these weaknesses in their ISA260 report for 2024/25 as critical issues affecting financial sustainability. The DSG deficit is a long-standing pressure; whilst the Government committed on 9th February 2026 to resolve 90% of authorities' accumulated deficits, internal audit coverage identified that stronger joint working between Finance and Education teams is required to address control gaps.
findings.matters: An inability to develop sufficient savings plans is a fundamental financial control weakness that directly threatens the Council's long-term financial sustainability and its ability to manage deficits—both critical indicators of lending risk.
findings.figures: Government will resolve 90% of DSG deficits accrued to end of 2025/26; action plan required for Finance/Education joint working
findings.quote: The Council's external auditors, Grant Thornton, in their ISA260 report for 2024/25, highlighted in relation to financial sustainability "two significant weakness in relation to the council's ability to develop sufficient savings plans and its ability to manage and reduce the Dedicated Schools Grant deficit"

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item No 5 Appendix A - Annual Internal Audit Report and Opinion 2025
findings.headline: Control environment rated Moderate Assurance rather than Substantial, indicating medium-level risks in governance and internal control framework
findings.detail: The Chief Internal Auditor concluded that Moderate Assurance can be given over the adequacy and effectiveness of the Council's control environment for 2025/26. This represents a meaningful gap from higher assurance levels and reflects that controls are not consistently operating as intended. The rating is based on work covering 76 audits, of which 58% received Moderate Assurance opinions, 34% Good, 5% Substantial, and 3% Limited.
findings.matters: A Moderate Assurance rating signals persistent control weaknesses that affect the Council's financial governance, risk management capability, and overall control environment credibility—all material to assessments of financial stability.
findings.figures: Moderate Assurance given for 2025/26; 58% of audits rated Moderate, 34% Good, 5% Substantial, 3% Limited
findings.quote: It is my opinion that Moderate Assurance can be given over the adequacy and effectiveness of the Council's control environment for 2025/26

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item No 4 Appendix A - External Auditors Annual Report
findings.headline: IFRS 16 leases not yet fully identified; risk of material unrecognised commitments
findings.detail: IFRS 16 became mandatory for local authorities in 2024/25. The council is still in the process of identifying all arrangements in scope. If not all leases are identified, liabilities will be understated and the council's committed expenditure misrepresented.
findings.matters: IFRS 16 requires all lease commitments to be capitalised. Hidden or unrecognised leases mean the financial position is more stretched than reported, affecting both revenue budget and capital valuations.
findings.figures: None provided; implementation still in progress
findings.quote: Our review of the implementation of IFRS16 in 2024/25 at the Council identified that officers are still in the process of identifying and reviewing all arrangements that fall under the scope of IFRS16. There is therefore a risk that not all arrangements have been identified and recognised within the Council's financial statements.

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item No 4 Appendix A - External Auditors Annual Report
findings.headline: Audit fee up 27% to £822,940; prior year disclaimer of opinion not yet lifted
findings.detail: The audit fee has risen from £650,000 to £822,940. The council received a disclaimer of opinion in 2024/25 due to the audit backstop, meaning the auditor could not form any opinion on the financial statements. This has not been resolved for 2025/26.
findings.matters: A disclaimer of opinion (no assurance given) is typically a breach of lending covenants and signals financial statements are unverifiable. The fee increase reflects extra work needed to clear prior-year issues and meet tighter deadlines.
findings.quote: Our proposed fee for the audit is £822,940 (PY: £650,000) for the Council

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item No 4 Appendix A - External Auditors Annual Report
findings.headline: Cash accounting errors in prior year: cash balances incorrectly classified as debtors
findings.detail: The auditor identified material errors in the 2024/25 financial statements where cash was incorrectly included within debtors, and bank reconciliations could not be completed due to missing evidence. This is a significant risk for 2025/26 and suggests weak controls over cash management and record-keeping.
findings.matters: If a council cannot accurately report its cash position, basic solvency and liquidity are unverifiable. This goes to the heart of financial controls and is a red flag for lenders.
findings.figures: Cash balances being incorrectly included within debtors; bank reconciliations unable to be completed at backstop date
findings.quote: Our testing in 2024/25 identified a number of issues in relation to the cash balance reported in the financial statements. This included cash balances being incorrectly included within debtors. We were also unable to complete our testing of the bank reconciliations due to outstanding evidence at the backstop date.

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item No 4 Appendix A - External Auditors Annual Report
findings.headline: £74m in capital grants (s106) could not be evidenced or tested in prior year audit
findings.detail: In 2024/25, the auditor was unable to test £74.127m of s106 planning obligations due to lack of supporting evidence. S106 funds are held in trust and must be spent to specific conditions; untested balances represent unverified liabilities. This is flagged as a significant risk for 2025/26.
findings.matters: Unverified s106 balances signal poor financial control and record-keeping, and may represent commitments the council cannot meet, creating contingent liabilities that lenders cannot assess.
findings.figures: £74.127m of s106 arrangements unable to be tested due to lack of supporting evidence on individual arrangement basis
findings.quote: In 2024/25 we were unable to test £74.127m relating to s106 arrangement as evidence could not be provided on an individual arrangement basis.

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item No 4 Appendix A - External Auditors Annual Report
findings.headline: Finance team lacks capacity to deliver statutory financial reporting on time and to standard
findings.detail: The auditor has identified a significant weakness in the council's governance relating to capacity and resilience within the finance team. The council is required to deliver draft accounts by 30 June and audited accounts by 31 January 2027 (backstop date). Prior year audit failings in working papers and account closure were attributed to this resource constraint.
findings.matters: If the finance team cannot deliver clean accounts on time, the auditor may issue a disclaimer of opinion (no assurance given), which breaks covenant requirements for many lenders and signals that the council's financial position is unverifiable.
findings.figures: Prior year: draft accounts deadline 30 June 2026; audited accounts backstop 31 January 2027
findings.quote: reviews the capacity and resilience within the finance team and ensure sufficient resources are in place to support statutory financial reporting; and reviews the year end closedown processes to ensure all Officers are aware of their responsibilities

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item No 4 Appendix A - External Auditors Annual Report
findings.headline: Dedicated Schools Grant deficit spiraling to £69m by end of 2026/27, growing unchecked
findings.detail: The DSG deficit, a statutory overspend in schools funding, is forecast at £45m by end of 2025/26 and rising to over £69m by end of 2026/27. Despite governance improvements, the auditor has not confirmed these have arrested the growth. The deficit is a charge against reserves and an unsustainable draw on council resources.
findings.matters: A DSG deficit is a statutory obligation that cannot be passed to schools; it sits permanently on the council's balance sheet and consumes reserves. A £69m liability signals structural underfunding or overspend in a major service area that the council cannot control.
findings.figures: Forecast cumulative DSG deficit of £45m by end of 2025/26, rising to over £69m by end of 2026/27
findings.quote: There is a forecast cumulative DSG deficit of £45m by the end of 2025/26, rising to over £69m by the end of 2026/27.

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item No 4 Appendix A - External Auditors Annual Report
findings.headline: Medium-term budget gap of £27.5m by 2029/30 with no agreed savings plan to bridge it
findings.detail: The council is forecast to overspend its 2025/26 budget by £15.4m in Q3, and the auditor has identified delivery of savings to bridge medium-term budget gaps as a risk of significant weakness. The council has not yet developed sufficient income generation or savings schemes with minimal reliance on reserves.
findings.matters: A lender needs to know whether the council can balance its budget through its own efforts or will have to raid reserves, which depletes available liquidity and borrowing capacity.
findings.figures: Q3 2025/26 forecast overspend of £15.442m; cumulative funding gap of £13.659m for 2027/28, £19.286m for 2028/29, and £27.524m for 2029/30
findings.quote: MTFP reports cumulative funding gaps of £13.659m for the 2027/28 year, £19.286m for 2028/29 and for 2029/30 year the gap is £27.524m.

findings.paper_title: Executive Report - Draft Asset Management Strategy
findings.headline: Capital investment need for the housing stock may exceed available HRA resources.
findings.detail: The strategy will direct capital investment based on updated stock condition surveys (85% of stock now has recent survey data, with 1,600 properties surveyed annually). The council explicitly identifies a risk that the investment needs identified by these surveys could exceed resources available in the Housing Revenue Account. If this occurs, the capital programme would require further review. All borrowing must meet Prudential Code requirements.
findings.matters: A funding gap between identified capital needs and HRA resources signals potential pressure on the council's ability to maintain housing stock to required standards and could require additional borrowing or reprioritsation.
findings.figures: Over 8,000 homes; over 85% of stock has in-date survey; approximately 1,600 properties surveyed annually
findings.quote: The investment in the existing stock will be based on updated Stock Condition Survey reports – there is a risk that the investment need is greater than resources – if this were the case a further review of the capital programme would be undertaken.

findings.paper_title: Finance and Performance Report 205-26 Draft Outturn
findings.headline: Council tax collection performance below target for second consecutive year
findings.detail: The council notes that council tax collection has not met target at year-end, a position that repeated from the prior year. Business rates collection did meet target. The sustained shortfall suggests a structural issue with council tax collection rather than a one-year anomaly.
findings.matters: Repeated council tax collection misses signal resilience issues in the council's income base and debt recovery; a lender would view this as a risk to ongoing revenue stability.
findings.figures: Council tax collection below target; position repeated from prior year
findings.quote: Business Rates collection has met target, however council tax collection has not. This is a similar position to last year.

findings.paper_title: Finance and Performance Report 205-26 Draft Outturn
findings.headline: Demand-led pressures in adult social care, children's services and transport unresolved despite year-long management interventions
findings.detail: Throughout 2025/26, management and executive directors sought mitigating actions against identified demand pressures. These pressures remained material drivers of the year-end overspend. The council explicitly identifies these as ongoing risks to the budget.
findings.matters: Services that consistently overspend despite active management signal structural demand or unit cost problems; these are operational risks that may require service changes or additional funding to resolve.
findings.figures: £13.775m overspend driven by these pressures
findings.quote: The main risks identified included demand led services such as Adult Social Care, Children's Services, and Home to School Transport... Where any variances or emerging pressures were identified during the year then mitigating actions were sought

findings.paper_title: Finance and Performance Report 205-26 Draft Outturn
findings.headline: Capital programme experiencing material slippage across both general fund and housing revenue account
findings.detail: The general fund capital programme shows £18.4m of slippage and £20.5m total underspend. The housing revenue account has £10.7m of slippage. The council notes that cost of living inflation has driven material cost pressures and extended lead times, forcing reviews of project scope to stay within budget.
findings.matters: Slippage suggests difficulty in delivering capital schemes on time and budget, often a sign of inflation and cost volatility that could continue and constrain future delivery or require scope reductions.
findings.figures: GF capital slippage: £18.4m; total GF underspend: £20.5m; HRA capital slippage: £10.7m
findings.quote: General Fund Capital Programme – Underspend of £20.5m, with slippage of £18.4m... the current 'Cost of Living Crisis' has driven up the level of inflation... reductions to the scope of projects may be required

findings.paper_title: Finance and Performance Report 205-26 Draft Outturn
findings.headline: Dedicated Schools Grant deficit expanded by £2.374m to £21.784m in a single year
findings.detail: The DSG deficit for 2025/26 increased from the budgeted £19.410m to £21.784m as outturn. This deterioration of £2.374m in a single year means the accumulated DSG pressure is growing. The council is managing this as a continuing liability.
findings.matters: A growing DSG deficit is a known structural pressure across councils; a worsening position signals demographic or unit cost pressures that will continue to impact future budgets and borrowing capacity.
findings.figures: DSG deficit: £19.410m budgeted, £21.784m outturn (increase of £2.374m)
findings.quote: The original DSG Budget for 2025/26 had a budget deficit of £19.410m. The forecast outturn is an increase of £2.374m resulting in an overall deficit of £21.784m.

findings.paper_title: Finance and Performance Report 205-26 Draft Outturn
findings.headline: General Fund revenue overspend of £13.775m funded from smoothing reserves
findings.detail: The council recorded a £13.775m overspend in 2025/26. This is being covered by drawing on smoothing reserves. The overspend reflects unmet demand-led pressures in adult social care, children's services and home to school transport that management interventions during the year did not fully offset.
findings.matters: An overspend of this scale that relies on reserve drawdown reduces financial headroom and signals structural budget pressures that may recur.
findings.figures: £13.775m overspend; funded from smoothing reserves
findings.quote: General Fund - overspend of £13.775m... Approve the use of the smoothing reserves to fund the £13.775m draft outturn position.

findings.paper_title: Item 5 - Appendix C - NNC Audit Findings (ISA260) Report 2024-25 - Final
findings.headline: Inherited payables and receivables from predecessor council remain unidentified after 4 years
findings.detail: On local government reorganisation, West Northamptonshire Council took responsibility for managing payables and receivables inherited from predecessor bodies. A two-year project is underway to resolve these, but as of October 2025 there remain £35.146m in unidentified debtors and £28.805m in unidentified creditors (net position £6.341m). North Northamptonshire's share of this risk is approximately 50%, meaning roughly £3.2m of unidentified balances.
findings.matters: After four years, unidentified balances of this size suggest poor financial control and reconciliation processes inherited from the merger. North's share of £3.2m of unidentified balances creates contingent liability risk and clouds the true position of receivables/payables.
findings.figures: £35.146m unidentified debtors; £28.805m unidentified creditors; net £6.341m; North's share approximately 50%
findings.quote: At October 2025 these officers believe these figures are £35.146m of unidentified debtors and £28.805m of unidentified creditors (net position £6.341m). North's share of this balance could potentially be around 50%.

findings.paper_title: Item 5 - Appendix C - NNC Audit Findings (ISA260) Report 2024-25 - Final
findings.headline: Minimum Revenue Provision benefit expires in 2026/27, creating future budget pressure
findings.detail: The council is currently offsetting £6.154m of MRP charges annually against an overprovision built up by the predecessor County Council before reorganisation. This benefit runs out in 2026/27. From 2027/28, the council forecasts annual MRP charges of £5.203m (a decrease in this case, but the point is the benefit disappears). This forecast is built into the Medium Term Financial Plan.
findings.matters: The expiry of this offset creates a known change in the council's debt repayment charges. This affects budgets from 2026/27 onwards and needs to be factored into medium-term financial planning and borrowing capacity.
findings.figures: Current MRP benefit (offsetting) £6.154m (24/25); overprovision runs out 2026/27; forecast 2027/28 MRP £5.203m
findings.quote: The Authority is currently benefitting from the offsetting of MRP charges relating to the County Council (24/25 £6.154m) against an overprovision built up by the County Council prior to reorganisation. This overprovision is due to run out in 2026/27. The annual MRP charge for supported and unsupported borrowing in 2027/28 is forecast to be £5.203m. This figure is built into the Councils MTFP.

findings.paper_title: Item 5 - Appendix C - NNC Audit Findings (ISA260) Report 2024-25 - Final
findings.headline: Multiple bank reconciliation failures; missing external bank confirmations
findings.detail: Beyond the school cash issue, auditors identified multiple other bank reconciliation problems: a legacy Corby bank account (£4.345m) with no supporting evidence for reconciling items; two maintained schools with £1.42m unexplained difference (reduced to £176k after investigation, caused by VAT treatment issues); and missing external confirmations from Lloyds and NatWest. Auditors were unable to complete testing due to backstop deadline.
findings.matters: Multiple unresolved bank reconciliation issues suggest pervasive cash management and control failures. Missing external bank confirmations is a fundamental audit control that should always be obtainable.
findings.figures: Legacy Corby account £4.345m; school reconciliation differences £1.42m declining to £176k
findings.quote: We have been unable to test the legacy Corby bank account reconciliation (£4.345m). The bank account has been closed during the year with the closing balance being transferred to the Council main bank account. Officers have been unable to provide evidence to support the reconciling items in the closing bank reconciliation.

findings.paper_title: Item 5 - Appendix C - NNC Audit Findings (ISA260) Report 2024-25 - Final
findings.headline: Investment property misclassification identified with £12.6m extrapolated error
findings.detail: In a sample of 11 investment property assets (£124m), auditors found 5 assets (£7.1m) had been incorrectly classified as investment properties when they should have been classified as other land and buildings. When extrapolated across the total population, the auditors estimate a potential misstatement of £12.6m. The council is now undertaking a full review of all investment properties.
findings.matters: Incorrect asset classification affects both the balance sheet presentation and may indicate poor fixed asset management. A £12.6m potential error is material and suggests weaknesses in asset accounting controls.
findings.figures: £7.1m identified error in sample; £12.6m estimated extrapolated error across population of investment properties
findings.quote: Officers identified that 5 of these assets (total value £7.1m) should have been classified as other land and buildings and not investment properties. We have extrapolated this error across the total population, with a potential misstatement of £12.6m.

findings.paper_title: Item 5 - Appendix C - NNC Audit Findings (ISA260) Report 2024-25 - Final
findings.headline: Section 106 contributions worth £74.1m cannot be tracked or audited
findings.detail: The council holds £74.127m in capital grants received in advance relating to section 106 agreements (developer contributions). Auditors were unable to audit this balance because officers cannot provide a breakdown by individual arrangement. This has been an unresolved issue since 2023/24. No audit testing could be completed on this balance.
findings.matters: Section 106 funds are restricted and must be spent in accordance with legal agreements. Inability to track £74m of these funds creates compliance risk, project delivery risk, and suggests poor governance over capital commitments. This could affect the council's ability to deliver promised infrastructure.
findings.figures: £74.127m in Capital Grants Received in Advance (s106 agreements)
findings.quote: Officers have been unable to provide a breakdown of this balance (£74.127m) by individual arrangement. We have therefore been unable to undertake any audit testing on this balance.

findings.paper_title: Item 5 - Appendix C - NNC Audit Findings (ISA260) Report 2024-25 - Final
findings.headline: School cash balances have not been reconciled for four years, creating £5.2m error
findings.detail: The council's school cash balance was not updated since 31 March 2021. Transactions were incorrectly mapped in the ledger and movements were included in debtors instead of cash, overstating cash by £5.237m and understating debtors by the same amount. This is a fundamental control failure in a material balance.
findings.matters: A four-year reconciliation failure for school cash suggests deeply broken financial controls. Schools represent significant cash holdings; inability to track them indicates poor governance and cash management risk.
findings.figures: £5.237m overstatement of cash; £5.237m understatement of debtors
findings.quote: The cash balance for schools had not been updated since 31 March2021 as the transactions were incorrectly mapped in the ledger. The movements since then have been incorrectly included within debtors. This resulted in the cash being overstated by £5.237m and debtors understated by the same amount.

findings.paper_title: Item 5 - Appendix C - NNC Audit Findings (ISA260) Report 2024-25 - Final
findings.headline: Finance function has capacity and resilience problems due to long-term staff sickness
findings.detail: Auditors note that the finance team has experienced unforeseen long-term sickness absence which has caused delays in responding to audit queries and providing evidence. The auditors explicitly flag this as highlighting 'a weakness in resilience and capacity within the Council's finance functions.' This underpins many of the other audit failures documented in this report.
findings.matters: If the finance team lacks capacity to respond to auditors, it suggests poor financial controls and reporting systems. Long-term sickness absence indicates vulnerability to key person risk and suggests the team may be understaffed for the council's complexity.
findings.figures: Unforeseen long-term sickness absence; capacity issues documented across multiple audit areas
findings.quote: Some of these delays we have encountered has been due to unforeseen long term sickness absence, which has accounted for some of the issues we have encountered it also highlights a weakness in resilience and capacity within the Council's finance functions.

findings.paper_title: Item 5 - Appendix C - NNC Audit Findings (ISA260) Report 2024-25 - Final
findings.headline: Auditors identify significant weaknesses in the council's value for money arrangements
findings.detail: Grant Thornton has completed its VFM work and identified significant weaknesses in the Authority's overall arrangements for securing economy, efficiency and effectiveness. The auditors explicitly state they are not satisfied that the council has made proper arrangements. This is more serious than routine audit findings and requires reporting in detail in a separate Auditor's Annual Report.
findings.matters: Significant VFM weaknesses indicate the council may not be deploying resources effectively or efficiently, which affects repayment capacity and debt sustainability. This is a red flag for lending decisions.
findings.figures: Significant weaknesses identified across economy, efficiency and effectiveness
findings.quote: We identified significant weaknesses in the Authority's arrangements and so are not satisfied that the Authority has made proper arrangements for securing economy, efficiency and effectiveness in its use of resources.

findings.paper_title: Item 5 - Appendix C - NNC Audit Findings (ISA260) Report 2024-25 - Final
findings.headline: Auditors will disclaim opinion on the financial statements entirely
findings.detail: The auditors cannot form an opinion on the financial statements and will issue a disclaimed audit opinion. This follows a disclaimed opinion in 2023/24 and means the council has now had no audited financial statements for two years. The auditors cite inability to obtain sufficient work on opening balances, in-year transactions, and year-end closing balances due to backstop legislation timing.
findings.matters: A disclaimed audit opinion means lenders cannot rely on independently verified financial statements. This makes credit assessment impossible and raises major governance concerns about financial control.
findings.figures: Backstop deadline 27 February 2026
findings.quote: Owing to the challenges of undertaking an audit where the previous years' audits were subject to backstop-related disclaimed audit opinions, we have been unable to undertake sufficient work to support an unmodified audit opinion in advance of the backstop date of 27 February 2026... we will be unable to form an opinion on the financial statements. Our anticipated financial statements audit report opinion will be a disclaimed opinion.

findings.paper_title: Item 7 - Appendix A - North Northamptonshire Council - Auditor's Annual Report 2024-25 - Final
findings.headline: Procurement waivers remain very high at 96 in 2024/25 (£5.2m) and 46 in first half of 2025/26 (£2.5m), with weak commissioning controls.
findings.detail: High waiver activity continues with weaknesses identified in commissioning practice for agency staff, consultants, and housing repairs. While controls including a Staffing Approval Panel and Spending Management Panel are being introduced, they are not yet fully embedded. Waiver data has not been routinely reported to Audit and Governance Committee.
findings.matters: High and increasing waiver activity suggests a loss of control over procurement processes and potential value-for-money risks through direct awards and non-competitive procurement.
findings.figures: 2024/25: 96 waivers totalling £5.2m. First half 2025/26: 46 waivers totalling £2.5m
findings.quote: Waiver activity remains high: 96 waivers totalling £5.2m in 2024/25 and 46 waivers totalling £2.5m in the first half of 2025/26

findings.paper_title: Item 7 - Appendix A - North Northamptonshire Council - Auditor's Annual Report 2024-25 - Final
findings.headline: Capital programme £58.6m underspend in 2024/25 with poor forecasting of project phasing.
findings.detail: The council spent £50.4m against a £108.9m capital budget, representing a £58.6m variance. While £48.7m is carried forward to 2025/26, a further £9.9m relates to projects that will not now proceed. The auditors note explanations are clear but the council needs to forecast phasing better.
findings.matters: Large capital slippage suggests issues with project delivery capacity or planning, which could affect the council's ability to complete investment programmes and realise intended service improvements or savings.
findings.figures: 2024/25 capital expenditure £50.4m, budget £108.9m, variance £58.6m, carry forward £48.7m, projects not proceeding £9.9m
findings.quote: In 2024/25 the Council incurred capital expenditure of £50.4m against a budget of £108.9m, a variance of £58.6m, of which £48.7m is to be carried forward into 2025/26. A further £9.9m relates to projects that will not now proceed

findings.paper_title: Item 7 - Appendix A - North Northamptonshire Council - Auditor's Annual Report 2024-25 - Final
findings.headline: Finance team capacity and resilience weakness identified after failures to provide audit evidence, with staff absences contributing to delays.
findings.detail: The auditors identified that long-term sickness in the finance team contributed to delays in providing audit evidence and queries, and that this reveals a fundamental weakness in capacity and resilience. The council is required to review finance team resources and year-end closedown processes.
findings.matters: Insufficient capacity to support statutory financial reporting and audit processes indicates the council may struggle to deliver timely, accurate financial information in future periods.
findings.figures: Audit delayed and key items untested due to staff absences; £74.127m balance unverified
findings.quote: Some of these delays have been due to long term sickness but it also highlights a weakness in resilience and capacity within the Council's finance functions

findings.paper_title: Item 7 - Appendix A - North Northamptonshire Council - Auditor's Annual Report 2024-25 - Final
findings.headline: Adult Social Care overspend of £5.9m in 2024/25 on demographic demand the council is struggling to manage.
findings.detail: Adult Social Care recorded a significant £5.9m overspend in the year under review. The 2025/26 budget includes £23.7m investment to allow for demand and cost increases, but this reflects acknowledged pressure on this statutory service.
findings.matters: Uncontrolled adult social care spending is a common precursor to financial stress in councils, and suggests demand or cost assumptions are not being met by budgetary planning.
findings.figures: 2024/25 Adult Social Care overspend £5.9m. 2025/26 investment allocation £23.7m
findings.quote: Adult Social Care where there is an overspend of £5.9m [Period 9 was £2.7m]

findings.paper_title: Item 7 - Appendix A - North Northamptonshire Council - Auditor's Annual Report 2024-25 - Final
findings.headline: Northamptonshire Children's Trust overspend increasing from £6.5m (2024/25) to forecast £8.67m (2025/26).
findings.detail: The shared trust's total overspend is worsening: £15.9m in 2024/25 (council's share £6.5m) forecast to increase to £19.64m in 2025/26 (council's share £8.67m). The overspend is driven by £10.9m of placement costs. Council is trying to manage through enhanced governance and supporting the trust to build in-house capacity.
findings.matters: Increasing uncontrolled spend by a delivery partner represents a material financial risk to the council that has required it to absorb overspends while managing overall finances.
findings.figures: 2024/25 NCT total overspend £15.9m (council share £6.5m), placement costs £10.9m. 2025/26 forecast NCT overspend £19.64m (council share £8.67m)
findings.quote: Northamptonshire Children's Trust (NCT) which reported a total overspend of £15.9m (Period 9 was £12.7m). The cost to the Council is £6.5m... NCT overspending is continuing, and increasing, in 2025/26. The total forecast overspend has increased from £12.76m at quarter one to £19.64m at quarter two.The Council's share wis £8.67m

findings.paper_title: Item 7 - Appendix A - North Northamptonshire Council - Auditor's Annual Report 2024-25 - Final
findings.headline: Dedicated Schools Grant cumulative deficit moving past £40m with 2025/26 forecast deficit of £18.7m.
findings.detail: The cumulative DSG deficit was £21.4m at 31 March 2025 and is forecast to reach over £40m by March 2026. In-year overspending continues despite council actions. While government has extended the statutory override allowing this to be treated as a negative reserve until 31 March 2028, it represents ongoing draw on council resources.
findings.matters: The DSG deficit is a material draw on reserves and represents uncontrolled demand pressures in special educational needs that could require exceptional financial support.
findings.figures: 2024/25 DSG deficit outturn £14.5m, cumulative £21.4m at 31 March 2025, 2025/26 forecast deficit £18.7m, cumulative forecast over £40m
findings.quote: The draft 2024/25 financial statements show a cumulative DSG deficit of £21.4m. The forecast outturn deficit for 2025/26 is £18.7m... The cumulative DSG deficit at 31 March 2025 was £21.4m, so this would take it past £40m

findings.paper_title: Item 7 - Appendix A - North Northamptonshire Council - Auditor's Annual Report 2024-25 - Final
findings.headline: Medium-term financial plan shows unsustainable budget gaps of £33m (2026/27), £53m (2027/28) and £73.6m (2028/29).
findings.detail: Despite achieving 90% of planned £25.2m savings in 2024/25, the council faces escalating funding gaps over the medium term that far exceed available reserves. Transformation plan is still work in progress. Available reserves of £80.9m (including smoothing reserve of £33.4m) are insufficient to cover forecast gaps.
findings.matters: Lenders need to understand whether the council has realistic plans to close these gaps or whether they will require exceptional financial support or unsustainable reserve depletion.
findings.figures: Gap 2026/27: £33m; 2027/28: £53m; 2028/29: £73.6m. General Fund reserve £23.4m, Earmarked Reserves £116.8m
findings.quote: The gap in 2026/27 is £33m, in 2027/28 £53m and in 2028/29 £73.6m. Available reserves are therefore insufficient to meet the forecast gap

findings.paper_title: Item 7 - Appendix A - North Northamptonshire Council - Auditor's Annual Report 2024-25 - Final
findings.headline: Auditors issued a disclaimed opinion and identified significant audit evidence gaps including inability to test £74.127m of S.106 agreements.
findings.detail: The council's auditors disclaimed their audit opinion after encountering significant difficulties obtaining audit trails, evidence for balances, and property valuations. Key items including school income and expenditure, cash, debtors, and the DSG remain untested. The auditors note that lack of improvement in 2026 will likely result in statutory recommendations.
findings.matters: A disclaimed audit opinion means the auditors cannot verify the accuracy of the council's financial statements, which undermines confidence in reported financial position and reserves available for debt service.
findings.figures: S.106 balance of £74.127m, property valuations £541.0m (land and buildings) and £219.8m (investment property)
findings.quote: we encountered significant difficulties in obtaining appropriate audit trails and evidence for balances included in the financial statements... we were unable to obtain a breakdown of the S.106 agreements balance (£74.127m) included in Capital Grants Received in Advance

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 07 - General Fund Report 2026-27
findings.headline: Corporate contingency of £2.4m provides minimal buffer against a £432.469m budget
findings.detail: The council has set aside only £2.4m as Corporate Contingency (0.55% of total net spend). Against a budget facing 'unprecedented financial challenges' and described as containing 'high budget delivery risks', this contingency is very tight and leaves limited room to absorb unexpected pressures or savings shortfalls.
findings.matters: Minimal contingency reserve signals limited financial resilience; any material savings non-delivery or demand overspend would require emergency reserve drawdown
findings.figures: £2.4m contingency; £432.469m total net spend
findings.quote: The Council has a Corporate Contingency of £2.4m

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 07 - General Fund Report 2026-27
findings.headline: Adult Social Care and Children's Services budgets remain uncertain and flagged for continued close monitoring
findings.detail: The budget requires £17.7m investment in Adult Social Care and £12.2m in Children's Services (Northamptonshire Children's Trust). The document explicitly flags these as high-risk demand-driven areas affected by 'increased complexity' and 'ongoing challenges in the health service'. Three separate scrutiny sessions were held in November to examine them, and the council will 'closely monitor and review again prior to the Final Budget', indicating uncertainty even at this late stage.
findings.matters: Demand-driven budgets frequently overspend when demand or complexity exceeds assumptions; flagging for post-budget review suggests estimates may not hold
findings.figures: £17.7m Adult Social Care investment; £12.2m Children's Services investment
findings.quote: The budget in key areas of demand such as Adult and Children's Social Care and homelessness has been significantly impacted by increased complexity, the ongoing challenges in the health service and external markets and the wider economic climate, so these budgets will be closely monitored and reviewed again prior to the Final Budget

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 07 - General Fund Report 2026-27
findings.headline: Funding settlement has reduced below estimated need; MTFP changed materially in less than a year
findings.detail: The council states that changes to government funding formulas and methodology have resulted in reduced funding below what it estimates it needs. The Medium-Term Financial Plan has undergone 'significant changes' compared to the position modelled 'just less than a year ago', driven by 'increasing demands'. The council must plan in 'unprecedented and challenging economic climate with continued uncertainty' which creates 'high budget delivery risks'.
findings.matters: Shows the council's funding assumptions are deteriorating, making medium-term financial forecasts unreliable and highlighting structural underfunding relative to service demand
findings.figures: Core Spending Power increases 14.5% by 2028-29 including Council Tax (only 8% without); Adult Social Care pressures £17.7m, Children's Services £12.2m
findings.quote: Changes in funding assumptions and methodology, has resulted in reduced funding reflecting the needs and demands of North Northamptonshire, now makes the task of planning how the Council will use its financial resources in an unprecedented and challenging economic climate with continued uncertainty around funding into the medium-term results in high budget delivery risks and makes informed medium term financial planning incredibly difficult

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 07 - General Fund Report 2026-27
findings.headline: DSG deficit liability will fall on the council from 2028-29 when government support ends
findings.detail: The government will fund 90% of local authorities' Dedicated Schools Grant deficits through a High Needs Stability Grant, but only until the end of 2027-28. After 31 March 2028, the Statutory Override ends and North Northamptonshire must fund the residual DSG deficit entirely from its own resources. The council has only three years to set aside reserves to meet this obligation.
findings.matters: Creates a hard financial obligation materially affecting the council's reserve strategy and balance sheet from 2028-29 onwards
findings.figures: 90% of DSG deficits covered until end of 2027-28; residual deficit payable from reserves from 2028-29
findings.quote: The Statutory Override will end on 31 March 2028. Therefore, local authorities will need to plan to be able to meet the cost of the residual deficit from their own resources in 2028-29, including setting aside appropriate reserves in the preceding years

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 09 - Appendix D - Investment Strategy 2026-27
findings.headline: £19.755m held in out-of-area commercial property with acknowledged liquidity constraints and annual strategic review
findings.detail: The council holds £19.755m in out-of-area commercial property investments at book value. Property is explicitly described as 'relatively difficult to sell and convert to cash at short notice' and may 'take a considerable period to sell in certain market conditions'. The council commits to annual review of strategic value and will commence disposal if deemed no longer strategically necessary.
findings.matters: A material holding in illiquid assets requires scrutiny given the 89% contraction in operational cash forecasts. Any unexpected liquidity need could create pressure to sell property in market conditions where sales may be difficult or value-destructive.
findings.figures: Out-of-area investment properties: £19.755m (purchase cost and book value), 4.69% net rate of return, with £555k gain forecast for 2025/26
findings.quote: Compared with other investment types, property is relatively difficult to sell and convert to cash at short notice and can take a considerable period to sell in certain market conditions.

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 09 - Appendix D - Investment Strategy 2026-27
findings.headline: Treasury management investments forecast to decline 89% from £137.963m to £14.936m between 2024/25 and 2026/27
findings.detail: The council's treasury management investments (surplus cash held for operational purposes) are forecast to contract sharply from £137.963m actual in 2024/25, through £59.537m forecast for 2025/26, to £14.936m budgeted for 2026/27. This represents a material reduction in the council's liquid cash reserves. The document provides no explanation for the cause of this decline.
findings.matters: A lender needs to understand whether this reflects structural changes in the council's financial position, reduced income, increased spending, or changed cash management approach. A 90% decline in operational cash reserves over two years is material to credit assessment and raises questions about the council's cash generation and liquidity.
findings.figures: Treasury management investments: £137.963m (2024/25 actual), £59.537m (2025/26 forecast), £14.936m (2026/27 budget)
findings.quote: The balance of treasury management investments is expected to fluctuate between £14.9m and £131.1m during the 2026/27 financial year.

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 08 - HRA Draft Budget 2026-27
findings.headline: Capital investment needs may exceed available resources, with no contingency funding strategy if shortfall occurs
findings.detail: The council notes that capital investment needs will be based on updated Stock Condition Survey reports. The document explicitly flags risk that investment need will exceed resources and states that 'a further review of the capital programme would be undertaken', but provides no contingency funding strategy if this materialises.
findings.matters: Insufficient capital to maintain the housing stock could lead to regulatory breaches (Decent Homes Standard), service deterioration, or forced additional borrowing, all of which constrain the council's financial flexibility.
findings.figures: No quantification provided
findings.quote: There is a risk that the investment need is greater than resources – if this were the case a further review of the capital programme would be undertaken.

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 08 - HRA Draft Budget 2026-27
findings.headline: Fire safety and health & safety compliance changes flagged as creating unquantified additional cost pressures over medium term
findings.detail: The council explicitly identifies that compliance with changing health and safety legislation, particularly fire safety requirements, will present additional challenges over the next few years and could lead to increased costs. These risks are not quantified or budgeted for, suggesting they may materialise during the 2027-31 medium-term period.
findings.matters: Unbudgeted regulatory compliance costs could force budget deficits or require service cuts to maintain balanced positions. Fire safety remediation has proved costly for councils across England.
findings.figures: No quantification provided
findings.quote: Compliance with regulatory standards and changes to health and safety legislation particularly regarding fire safety will provide additional challenges over the next few years and could lead to increased costs.

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 08 - HRA Draft Budget 2026-27
findings.headline: Minimum reserves set at £2.23m (5% of budget), providing limited contingency for adverse variances
findings.detail: The council has aligned minimum reserve levels to 5% of total HRA budget, with minimum reserves increasing from £2.1m to £2.23m. This represents a tight reserve buffer for an account managing 8,081 properties, £91.821m debt, and multiple identified risks including rent collection deterioration, unquantified fire safety costs, and potentially insufficient capital investment resources.
findings.matters: Low reserves constrain the council's ability to absorb adverse variances (unexpected maintenance, rent shortfalls, regulatory compliance costs) without external funding or service cuts.
findings.figures: £2.23m minimum reserves, 5% of total budget
findings.quote: The Executive Director of Finance has assessed that the minimum level of balances, taking all known risks into account and has aligned the retained minimum level of reserves to 5% of total budget. The minimum balances will be amended from £2.1m to £2.23m for the HRA.

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 08 - HRA Draft Budget 2026-27
findings.headline: Rent arrears explicitly identified as a main area of risk due to cost of living pressures and Universal Credit impacts
findings.detail: The council identifies rent arrears and debt collection as the main risk to HRA finances going forward. Specific concerns are flagged about tenants' ability to pay due to the current economic climate and cost of living pressures. Universal Credit is identified as a particular risk that could further increase rent arrears. Bad debts provision remains at £0.439m for 2026-27.
findings.matters: Rental income of £43m is the sole funding source for all HRA services and debt service. Rising arrears would reduce cash collections, forcing reserve drawdowns or spending cuts to maintain the required balanced budget.
findings.figures: £43m annual rental income, £0.439m bad debts provision 2026-27
findings.quote: One of the main areas of risk for the HRA going forward is rent arrears and the management of debt within the rent account. There is a specific risk around the ability to collect this debt as a result of the current economic climate and the pressures on tenants from the cost of living.

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 08 - HRA Draft Budget 2026-27
findings.headline: HRA debt of £91.821m with £3.291m annual interest costs represents a material fixed obligation
findings.detail: North Northamptonshire HRA carries substantial debt inherited from the 2012 self-financing settlement. The council budgets £3.291m for interest costs in 2026-27 against outstanding debt of £91.821m expected at year end. The document notes that HRA borrowing caps were lifted in 2018, leaving scope for further borrowing subject to Prudential Code affordability tests.
findings.matters: Debt service is a fixed cost that must be covered from rental income. Any deterioration in collection rates or unexpected cost increases could compromise debt servicing and force either reserve drawdowns or service cuts.
findings.figures: £91.821m outstanding debt, £3.291m interest budget 2026-27, combined Corby/Kettering 2012 settlement debt £143.5m
findings.quote: The 2026/27 budget for the Housing Revenue Account provides for £3.291m to cover interest costs. The outstanding debt is estimated to be £91.821m at the end of March 2027.

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 09 - Appendix B - Treasury Management Strategy Statement 2026-27
findings.headline: Investment balances expected to decline as council consumes reserves to fund capital programme
findings.detail: Investment balances that ranged between £132.9m and £203.7m in the previous year are forecast to decline in 2026/27 due to both debt repayment and using internal resources to fund the capital programme. This consumption of liquid reserves reduces the council's financial buffer.
findings.matters: Lower cash reserves limit the council's ability to absorb spending volatility or unplanned costs; reduces financial flexibility in a period of economic uncertainty and public expenditure cuts
findings.figures: Previous investment balance range £132.9m to £203.7m; 2026/27 forecast shows decline
findings.quote: Due to debt repayment and further internal resources used to fund the capital programme, it is expected that investment balances will be lower in 2026/27.

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 09 - Appendix B - Treasury Management Strategy Statement 2026-27
findings.headline: Council will be forced to borrow up to £27m over forecast period due to capital programme and minimal investment reserves
findings.detail: Despite holding £154.2m in treasury investments as of end-2025, the council's capital financing requirement is increasing while investment position is minimal. The strategy states the council will therefore need to externally borrow up to £27m over the medium-term forecast, a shift from previous position of being investment-positive.
findings.matters: Shows transition to borrowing-dependent position; increases total debt burden and future debt servicing obligations; reduces financial resilience
findings.figures: £154.2m treasury investments at 31/12/2025; requires £27m new external borrowing over forecast period
findings.quote: The Authority has an increasing CFR due to the capital programme, but minimal investments and will therefore be required to borrow up to £27m over the forecast period.

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 09 - Appendix B - Treasury Management Strategy Statement 2026-27
findings.headline: £32m of LOBO loans face refinancing in 2026/27 with high probability lenders will exercise rate increase options
findings.detail: The council holds £32m of LOBO (Lender's Option Borrower's Option) loans where the lender can propose interest rate increases at set dates. With long-term interest rates having risen, the strategy explicitly states there is now a good chance that lenders will exercise their options during 2026/27. If they do, the council must either accept higher rates or repay the loan.
findings.matters: Creates material upside risk to annual debt servicing costs; forces a costly choice between accepting rate increases or accelerated debt repayment with no current plan for how to fund it
findings.figures: £32m of LOBO loans with options exercisable during 2026/27
findings.quote: £32m of these LOBO loans have options during 2026/27, and with long-term interest rates having risen in recent years, there is now a good chance that lenders will exercise their options.

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 07 - Appendix A - Budget 202627 and Medium Term Financial Plan
findings.headline: Council acknowledges transformation is required but has not yet detailed how unplanned budget gaps will be closed
findings.detail: The Executive Summary repeatedly states the council is 'focused upon the achievement of financial sustainability' and that 'further transformation and change in targeted areas will be required'. However, the plan does not identify specific, quantified transformation projects that would close the £13.7m–£27.5m gaps. The document mentions feasibility studies, new systems, and AI adoption as under-way, but these are not quantified against the deficit.
findings.matters: A council explicitly relying on transformation to close a gap must present the transformation plan with realistic deliverable savings. Lenders need confidence that identified solutions exist, not just that transformation is intended.
findings.figures: Unquantified budget gaps 2027/28–2029/30: £60.469m cumulative
findings.quote: It is acknowledged that further transformation and change in targeted areas will be required to ensure the Council delivers the right outcomes and remains financially sustainable over the medium term... A number of activities, including a feasibility study into Extra Care provision... have been progressed and are being delivered within Adult Social Care

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 07 - Appendix A - Budget 202627 and Medium Term Financial Plan
findings.headline: 2026/27 budget balanced by drawing £6.567m from reserves and £2.5m flexible capital receipts
findings.detail: The council achieves a balanced 2026/27 budget partly through reserve drawdown (£6.567m) and use of flexible use of capital receipts (£2.5m). The MTFP assumes no further reserve support from 2027/28 onwards, but given the emerging budget gaps, this assumption appears optimistic.
findings.matters: Using reserves to balance a budget in year 1 of the MTFP, then expecting to stop in year 2 while gaps grow to £13.7m, signals unrealistic planning. Reserves are already being depleted to manage current-year pressure.
findings.figures: 2026/27 transfer from reserves: £6.567m; Flexible Use of Capital Receipts: £2.5m; total: £9.067m (2% of base budget)
findings.quote: Transfer to / (From) Reserves (6,567)... Flexible Use of Captial Receipts (FUCR) (2,500)

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 07 - Appendix A - Budget 202627 and Medium Term Financial Plan
findings.headline: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) funding of £8.915m is at risk of reduction or removal in future years
findings.detail: The 2026/27 budget includes £8.915m of EPR funding for waste recycling reforms. The council explicitly states: 'It is assumed that EPR funding continues at the same level from 2027-28 onwards when further announcements are made the MTFP will be updated accordingly, which could present a funding risk to the MTFP if reduced or removed.' This is a contingent, time-limited income source.
findings.matters: This is recurring funding treated as if it will continue, but the council has publicly acknowledged it may not. Loss of £8.915m would directly increase the budget gaps in years 2–4.
findings.figures: EPR 2026/27 funding: £8.915m
findings.quote: It is assumed that EPR funding continues at the same level from 2027-28 onwards when further announcements are made the MTFP will be updated accordingly, which could present a funding risk to the MTFP if reduced or removed.

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 07 - Appendix A - Budget 202627 and Medium Term Financial Plan
findings.headline: Council tax base growth of 1.5% (£3.2m) is critical to the budget but depends on housing development delivery
findings.detail: The 2026/27 budget assumes council tax base will grow from 117,585 to 119,354 (1.5% growth) based on 'planned developments'. The document then explicitly flags the risk: 'The risk if we do not see this increase would be felt in future years due to how Council Tax is accounted for.' This is a material dependency on development pipeline delivery.
findings.matters: A 1.5% growth assumption is material to a council of this size. If housing development stalls—due to market conditions, planning delays, or developer exits—the council loses recurring income with no offset identified.
findings.figures: Tax base growth: 1,769 properties (1.5%); income value: c£3.2m
findings.quote: The Council Tax base has increased by 1.5% (c£3.2m) based on planned developments – the risk if we do not see this increase would be felt in future years due to how Council Tax is accounted for.

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 07 - Appendix A - Budget 202627 and Medium Term Financial Plan
findings.headline: Funding withheld under Fair Funding Review phases: £3.9m in 2026/27, £1.95m in 2027/28
findings.detail: The government is phasing in the new funding allocations over three years. One-third of funding changes apply in 2026/27, two-thirds in 2027/28, and full changes in 2028/29. This creates a direct impact: £3.9m and £1.95m of expected funding is being deliberately held back, contributing to the budget pressure.
findings.matters: This is a known, direct headwind to the budget for two years. It is not a forecast risk but a stated government policy reducing available cash.
findings.figures: 2026/27 funding withheld: £3.9m; 2027/28 funding withheld: £1.95m
findings.quote: One-third of the changes in funding will be applied in 2026-27, two-thirds in 2027-28, and the full amount in 2028-29... The impact to NNC is that, based on our assumptions, funding of around £3.9m is withheld in 26/27 and £1.95m in 27/28.

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 07 - Appendix A - Budget 202627 and Medium Term Financial Plan
findings.headline: Business Rates baseline reset will eliminate the authority's previous above-average growth advantage
findings.detail: North Northamptonshire had benefitted from above-average business growth under the old retention system. The Fair Funding Review resets the baseline in 2026/27, and the document explicitly states this growth benefit 'will be wiped out'. Future growth will be measured from a lower starting point, materially reducing this income source.
findings.matters: This is a real loss of recurring income, not a forecast risk. It will persist for at least three years and signals reduced resilience to future shocks. It directly contributes to the budget gaps described above.
findings.figures: Business Rates Funding Baseline 2026/27: £88.016m (compared to £66.710m Business Rates Baseline, showing reset mechanics)
findings.quote: North Northamptonshire had benefitted well under the previous Business Rates Retention system due to an above average increase in business growth across its area... That will be wiped out when the new system is introduced in 2026/27 as the Business Rates Baseline – the point from growth will be re-set.

findings.paper_title: Agenda Item 07 - Appendix A - Budget 202627 and Medium Term Financial Plan
findings.headline: Budget gaps of £13.7m, £19.3m and £27.5m emerging in 2027/28–2029/30 with no identified solution
findings.detail: The council balances 2026/27 at £0m gap but faces cumulative unplanned deficits of £13.659m in 2027/28, £19.286m in 2028/29, and £27.524m in 2029/30. These will require either savings not yet identified, service reductions, or reserves drawdown—none of which are detailed in the plan.
findings.matters: An authority with growing structural deficits faces serious questions about service sustainability and debt serviceability. Lenders need to know whether these gaps are assumed to be solved by unspecified transformation, by depleting reserves, or by cuts.
findings.quote: The budget gap for NNC is shown on a cumulative basis.

news_drafts.lead: Unreconciled transactions of this age represent a potential control weakness and create risk of misstatement in the accounts or undetected fraud. The fact they remain unreconciled after a year suggests either control breakdowns or inadequate monitoring.
